safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention absence of neck stiffness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: In an acute severe headache, documenting absence of neck stiffness helps risk-stratify for meningitis/SAH and guides urgency of escalation. Omitting this negative red-flag element can lead to less safe handoffs and delayed reconsideration of serious causes.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention absence of fever.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Absence of fever is a key negative finding when assessing severe headache for infectious etiologies (e.g., meningitis) and other systemic illness. Failure to document it can impair downstream triage/decision-making and may prompt unnecessary escalation or missed re-evaluation triggers.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no nausea at present.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts do not mention absence of nausea.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Nausea/vomiting is clinically relevant for differentiating migraine versus other intracranial pathology and for monitoring deterioration. Omitting the absence of nausea reduces clarity of the headache phenotype and can lead to less targeted follow-up and safety-netting.
